records.text: Quaker Oats conducted experiments in which unsuspecting boys were fed radioactive oatmeal
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: Look at this article. This is our government. A spoonful of sugar helps the radioactive oatmeal go down. Yes, Quaker Oats was conducting experiments on unsuspecting young boys.

verification.notes: Transcript context reviewed. The federal ACHRE history confirms boys at Fernald were fed radioactive tracers in oatmeal and that Quaker Oats funded the research, but university scientists—not Quaker Oats itself—conducted the experiments.

sources.title: ACHRE Final Report, Chapter 7: The Fernald School
sources.relevance: Federal history identifies researchers, child subjects, radioactive oatmeal, and Quaker Oats funding.

records.text: The United States Atomic Energy Commission partnered with Quaker Oats to experiment on children
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: Yeah, I don't know what to say. Anyway, the Atomic Energy Commission teamed up with Quaker Oats to experiment on children.

verification.notes: Transcript context reviewed. The federal ACHRE history states the Atomic Energy Commission and Quaker Oats were among the funders of radioisotope experiments involving institutionalized children at Fernald.

sources.title: ACHRE Final Report, Chapter 7: The Fernald School
sources.relevance: Federal history documents AEC and Quaker Oats funding of experiments involving Fernald children.
